claims.text: YBa2Cu3O7−δ is a layered cuprate superconductor.
Systematic tuning of oxygen doping and lattice strain in YBa2Cu3O7−δ enhances superconductivity.
The enhancement occurs by optimizing electron-pairing interactions in the CuO2 planes.
Changing the oxygen doping level modifies carrier concentration.
Controlled lattice strain affects the local crystalline environment.
Substrate engineering can be used to impose lattice strain on YBa2Cu3O7−δ thin films.
The CuO2 planes are critical for electron pairing in layered cuprates.
Modifying oxygen content and strain alters the local electronic environment in the CuO2 planes.
The altered local electronic environment enhances electron-pairing interactions.
Oxygen content and strain affect both conventional electron–phonon coupling and additional unconventional pairing interactions.
Optimized oxygen doping and applied strain will increase the superconducting critical temperature relative to conventionally doped, unstrained YBa2Cu3O7−δ.
Optimized oxygen doping and applied strain will improve superconducting-state coherence relative to the baseline.
Excessive doping or strain may introduce phase separation.
Excessive doping or strain may introduce structural instabilities that compromise the integrity of the CuO2 planes and limit superconducting enhancement.
The magnitude of Tc enhancement and the relative contributions of electron–phonon and unconventional interactions are uncertain.
